ground_truth.location: Table 7, panel (a) Action-signaling model parameter estimates, Berkeley, gamma_1^a
ground_truth.context: Table 7 ("Structural estimates and tests of consistency"), panel (a), Berkeley row, first column: the linear coefficient of the quadratic structural public recognition utility of the action-signaling model, gamma_1 (a - rho abar) + gamma_2 (a - rho abar)^2 (Section 7.1, equation 5), with effort a in hundreds of points.  The structural parameters are functions of the reduced-form quadratic PRU r0 + r1 a + r2 a^2 estimated in Table 6, column (4) (OLS of stated WTP on the interval midpoint in hundreds of points and its square, the 1700+ interval excluded, Berkeley final sample), with the comparison population being the experimental sample's performance under public recognition (Section 7.1, Appendix F).  The table prints the full-sample point estimate with a bootstrapped percentile confidence interval (1,000 replications clustered by participant).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Prolific final sample is 970 participants (2910 participant-rounds), not the 968 stated in Section 6.1: applying the attention-check exclusion (7 failures) and the incoherent-preference exclusion (40, matching the paper's notes) leaves 970; no documented rule identifies the 2 further exclusions, so none were made.

The 'incoherent' rule is not spelled out for the charity experiments; it was operationalised on the yes/no preference-for-recognition pattern across the 18 intervals: coherent = weakly increasing (incl. constant) or single-peaked; decreasing, U-shaped and multi-switch patterns excluded. This reproduces the stated exclusion counts (40/11/2) and the 1.0/1.8/1.7% non-monotone shares.

Table 7 rho uses as reference average the anonymous-round mean plus the Table 5 col (2) public recognition effect (as described in the task), in hundreds of points; bootstrap CIs were not computed (point estimates only).
cell.notes: Exploratory attempts 1-2 inspected attention-check coding (non-missing = fail), round orders, and candidate coherence rules (no RESULT lines). Final: Table 5 = OLS of points on public-recognition and financial-incentive round dummies plus round-position dummies (first omitted), one obs per participant-round, SEs clustered by participant (fixest). BU = QM222 classroom file (121 completers); QM221 file not used. Signed WTP = pref_rec_X_1 if preference yes, minus pref_anom_X_1 if no (budget-constrained answers). Table 6 col (4) Berkeley: OLS of WTP on interval midpoint in hundreds of points and its square, 1700+ interval excluded (r0=-3.3246, r1=0.3790, r2=-0.00404). Structural (Appendix F.1): gamma1=sqrt(r1^2-4 r0 r2); rho=(sqrt(r1^2-4 r2 r0)-r1)/(2 abar r2); c=(r1+2 r2 (a0+tau))/tau; prediction=p/c with p=$0.50 per hundred points. While reading the paper text for methods, the extraction briefly displayed some BU rows of Table 7 (lines ~2780-2789); these were not used. Docker runs completed in under 2 s each; no hangs.
